candidate_findings.message: Each data request is served by allocating one buffer the size of the whole requested range. AVPlayer often asks for everything up to the end of the resource (requestsAllDataToEndOfResource), so a 30 MB clip allocates about 30 MB, then copies it again with `buffer[..bytesRead]`, then a third time in `NSData.FromArray`. This repeats on every seek. For a resource over 2 GB, `(int)dataRequest.RequestedLength` overflows to a negative value, `new byte[negative]` throws, the catch swallows it, and playback fails. There is only one `stream.Read` call with no loop, so streams that return partial reads (FileStream, network or decrypting streams) deliver less data than requested. Because all the work happens synchronously inside `ShouldWaitForLoadingOfRequestedResource` on a serial queue, cancellations cannot be delivered either. Fix: read and `Respond` in bounded chunks (for example 64 KB to 1 MB) in a loop, stop when `loadingRequest.IsCancelled`, and use long arithmetic for the length.

Read and seek errors are only written to Debug output, and `ShouldWaitForLoadingOfRequestedResource` then calls `loadingRequest.FinishLoading()` (line 35) anyway. That tells AVFoundation the request succeeded even though no data, or truncated data, was sent. The player then stalls or shows a vague parse error instead of the real cause, and the failure never reaches `MediaFailed` with a useful message. On failure, call `loadingRequest.FinishLoadingWithError(...)` with an NSError, and only call `FinishLoading()` after the data was actually delivered.

Non-seekable streams always fail to open. When the stream can't seek, `length` is `C.LengthUnset` (-1), and ExoPlayer usually opens with `dataSpec.Length == C.LengthUnset`, so `bytesRemaining` becomes -1. The check `if (bytesRemaining < 0)` then throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`. The unknown-length handling in `Read` can never run. The check should exclude `C.LengthUnset`, for example `bytesRemaining != C.LengthUnset && bytesRemaining < 0`. Otherwise non-seekable streams should be explicitly rejected and documented, since the description promises they work with limited functionality.

`currentStreamDataSourceFactory` (a managed `Java.Lang.Object` subclass) is disposed while ExoPlayer may still hold the old `ProgressiveMediaSource` that references it. Here it happens before `SetPlayerData`, which can await network artwork downloads for seconds while the old item keeps playing. It also happens in `CreateMediaItemFromStream` (lines 804-805) before `SetMediaSource` swaps the source. If the player thread calls `createDataSource()` on the disposed peer (for example when queuing the next period while looping), the runtime tries to re-create the peer through a missing `(IntPtr, JniHandleOwnership)` constructor and throws `NotSupportedException`. The factory owns no native resources, so just drop the reference, or dispose it only after the player has been given the new source.

`Stream.AsRandomAccessStream()` throws `NotSupportedException` for non-seekable streams. This runs after an `await` inside `async ValueTask PlatformUpdateSource`, and `MediaElementHandler.MapSource` discards that ValueTask, so the exception is lost. The element stays in its previous state, `MediaFailed` is never raised, and the user gets no feedback. Check `CanSeek` and report the problem through `MediaElement.MediaFailed`, or buffer the stream yourself.

`GetStreamContentType` only distinguishes QuickTime from 'everything else = public.mpeg-4'. MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC/ADTS and similar audio streams are reported to AVFoundation as MPEG-4, so their parsing fails, which contradicts the claim that iOS/macOS works with both audio and video. It also duplicates the more complete sniffing in the shared `StreamExtensions.GetMimeType`. Reuse the shared detection and map the MIME type to a UTI (for example `public.mp3`, `com.microsoft.waveform-audio`, `public.mpeg-4-audio`). The final `return "public.mpeg-4"` should also use `StreamAssetResourceLoader.DefaultContentType`.

For non-seekable streams, `ContentLength` is set to 0 and byte-range access is disabled. AVFoundation then treats the resource as empty, so playback fails with no clear error. Non-seekable streams can't work through this path, so reject them up front with a `MediaFailed` message rather than advertising a zero-length resource.

On Tizen, `NotSupportedException` is thrown synchronously from `PlatformUpdateSource`, which `MapSource` calls directly. Just setting `Source` therefore crashes the app from inside a property mapper. It also happens after `Player.Unprepare()` and `CurrentStateChanged(Opening)`, leaving the player unprepared and stuck in Opening. Report the limitation through `MediaElement.MediaFailed` and reset state instead of throwing from the mapper.

The description and docs advertise `MediaSource source = myStream;` and implicit assignment to `MediaElement.Source`, but neither compiles. C# only considers user-defined conversions declared on the source type, its base classes, or the target type itself, so an operator on the derived `StreamMediaSource` is ignored when the target is `MediaSource`. The existing string and Uri conversions are declared on `MediaSource` for this reason. Add `public static implicit operator MediaSource(Stream stream)` on `MediaSource`, or correct the documentation.

`FromStream` does not validate its argument, unlike `FromUri`, which calls `ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull`. `MediaSource.FromStream(null!)` silently creates a source with no stream, and every platform then quietly does nothing. Add `ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(stream)`. Returning `StreamMediaSource` here, while `FromFile`, `FromUri` and `FromResource` return `MediaSource`, is also inconsistent with the existing factory pattern.

Some signatures are too weak, and the result is passed straight to `WinMediaSource.CreateFromStream` as a content-type hint. Any stream whose first byte is 0x47 ('G') is classified as `video/mp2t`. The frame-sync check `0xFF 0xEx/0xFx` also matches ADTS AAC (0xFFF1/0xFFF9) and reports it as `audio/mpeg`. A wrong hint can send Media Foundation to the wrong handler. For MPEG-TS, require a sync byte at offset 188 as well (or at least several packets), and exclude the ADTS layer bits. For unknown content, consider returning `string.Empty`, as the existing Windows header path does, rather than `application/octet-stream`. Separately, the class summary says 'on Windows platform', but the file is shared.

`httpClient.GetStreamAsync` runs in an `async void` override outside any try/catch. The try/catch in `UpdateSourceStream` doesn't cover it, so opening the page offline, or getting an HTTP error, throws an unhandled exception and crashes the sample. `OnAppearing` also re-downloads the 30 MB file into memory every time the page reappears. Wrap the download in the same error handling, and consider loading it only once.

The sample disposes the `MemoryStream` while `MediaElement.Source` still points to it. `UpdateSourceStream` releases the old stream before the new copy finishes, and `OnDisappearing` runs before `OnNavigatedFrom` stops the player. In both cases the native player can keep reading a disposed stream on its background thread. This is the lifetime mistake the feature docs warn callers about. Set `MediaElement.Source = null` or stop playback before disposing. Also, the semaphore only covers the dispose: `UpdateSourceStream` and the null check in `ReleaseSourceStream` (line 255) run outside it, so overlapping calls (the initial download plus Open/Record Video) can leak or dispose the active stream.

The page implements `IAsyncDisposable` and is registered as transient (`AddHttpClient<MediaElementFromStreamPage>` plus `AddTransientWithShellRoute`). Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection tracks transient disposables in the scope that resolved them, so every navigation creates a page instance the container keeps until the app or window scope is disposed. `DisposeAsync` is effectively never called during normal navigation. Since cleanup already happens in `OnDisappearing`, drop `IAsyncDisposable` from the page to avoid the leak.

`CreateMediaItemFromStream` copies the metadata and artwork logic of `CreateMediaItem` line for line, so future fixes to one will be missed in the other. It could call `CreateMediaItem("stream://media", cancellationToken)` and then set the factory. Also, the dispose-then-null at lines 804-805 is immediately followed by another assignment, which makes it redundant.

The fallback runs when `detectInstallMethod()` returned "git", meaning a source checkout. In that case it hard-codes `npm-global` and offers to run `npm install -g @aoagents/ao@latest`. On a source install, `ao` is usually provided by `npm link` from `packages/ao`, which is a symlink at `{prefix}/lib/node_modules/@aoagents/ao`. A global npm install replaces that symlink, so the user's checkout gets silently swapped for a registry copy and the checkout itself is never updated. A missing script in a source checkout means the build is incomplete (for example, assets were not copied into dist). The right response is an error telling the user to rebuild (`pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli build`), not a switch to a different install method. The fallback also calls `handleNpmUpdate(opts)`, which prints "--skip-smoke and --smoke-only only apply to git source installs. Ignoring." even though this is a git install. A user who passed `--smoke-only` (no fetch or rebuild) then gets offered a full global reinstall.

Removing the `scripts/ao-update.sh` sentinel leaves `.git` four directories up as the only signal for a "git" install. The tests that guarded this were deleted ("returns 'unknown' when .git exists but scripts/ao-update.sh does not"). Now any non-node_modules copy of the CLI whose ancestor four levels up is an unrelated git repo is classified as "git". `ao update` then runs `ao-update.sh` with REPO_ROOT set to that repo, which runs `git fetch`/`git pull --ff-only origin main`, `pnpm install`, and `pnpm --filter ... clean/build` there. The sentinel should move to the new location (for example `packages/cli/src/assets/scripts/ao-update.sh` or `packages/ao/package.json`) rather than being dropped.

The script now lives at `packages/cli/{src,dist}/assets/scripts/`, but the default REPO_ROOT is still `$(dirname BASH_SOURCE)/..`. That resolves to the `assets/` directory, not the repo root or the package root. If AO_REPO_ROOT is unset (running the script directly, or any caller that doesn't inject the env), every layout check runs against the wrong directory. The new package-install auto-detection can then never match, because `assets/` has no `package.json` or `dist/index.js`. It is effectively dead code, since `runRepoScript` always sets AO_SCRIPT_LAYOUT anyway. The default should be computed relative to the new location (`../../..` from dist/assets/scripts for a package; the repo root is further up for a checkout).

After the move, the unchanged fallback `REPO_ROOT=$(dirname BASH_SOURCE)/..` points at `packages/cli/src/assets` (or `dist/assets`) instead of the repo root. Running the script directly without AO_REPO_ROOT now partly works and then fails. The `git rev-parse` check passes because the directory is inside the worktree, so `git pull` and `pnpm install`/build run. Then `cd "$REPO_ROOT/packages/ao"` fails and the smoke tests point at nonexistent paths. The update is left half-applied. The relative default needs updating to match the new depth.

The regex-escape pattern is written inside a `${...}` expression, so it is ordinary JS rather than string content, but it is double-escaped as if it were a string: `/[.*+?^${}()|[\\]\\\\]/g`. The character class closes after `[\\`, so the pattern only matches a special character followed by a literal `\\]`. In practice it never escapes anything. The test only passes because the checkout path happens to have no regex metacharacters. A path containing `(`, `+`, `[`, etc. will make the test fail or throw on an invalid regex. Use `/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g`.

The `rotate()` transform is added to canvas-engine's `ShapeLayer`, but nothing mounts that component. It is only re-exported from `packages/canvas-engine/src/index.ts`. `apps/web` (`app.tsx`, `community.tsx`, `world-map.tsx`, benchmark) draws shapes through `createDomRendererPlugin()`, i.e. `packages/dom-renderer/src/dom-shape-layer.tsx`, plus `GpuShapeLayer`. Neither `DomShapeLayer`'s `ShapeWrapper` nor its unknown-type fallback got the transform. As a result, in the real app the hit tests (`withRotation`) and the spatial index now treat shapes as rotated while they are still drawn unrotated. Clicking a visible corner of a rotated shape misses, and clicking empty space inside its rotated footprint selects it. Before this change, drawing and hit testing were both unrotated and at least agreed. Apply the transform in `DomShapeLayer` (wrapper and fallback), or have both layers share one wrapper. The unchecked manual test in the PR would have caught this.

rectangle, rounded-rect, ellipse and line also have a `gpuPrimitive`. When WebGPU is available (`createGpuRendererPlugin()` is in `basePlugins`), the GPU renderer claims these shapes and `DomShapeLayer` skips them. The GPU path ignores rotation: `rect.wgsl`/`rect.ts` never reads `params.w`, the shape-sdf pipeline has no rotation, and `lineGpuPrimitive` doesn't pass it. GPU hover detection and selection highlights also use the unrotated AABB. So even after the DOM layer is fixed, these shapes are drawn unrotated while their `hitTest` is now rotated. Either support rotation in the GPU pipelines or return `null` from `gpuPrimitive` when `safeRotation(data.rotation) !== 0`, so they fall back to DOM.

Double-click/edit detection in the `canvas:pointerdown` handler still calls the raw, unwrapped `hitTest`, while the registered definition now uses `withRotation(hitTest)`. For a rotated text shape, the select tool and the editing state machine now disagree. A click on the rotated area outside the unrotated box selects the shape but never enters editing. A click inside the unrotated box but outside the rotated shape sends `POINTER_DOWN` for a shape that wasn't hit. Create the wrapped function once (e.g. `const rotatedHitTest = withRotation(hitTest)`) and use it both here and in `register`.

Same problem as in the text plugin. Sticky's `canvas:pointerdown` edit detection calls the unwrapped `hitTest`, but the registered `hitTest` is `withRotation(hitTest)`. On rotated stickies, double-click-to-edit uses different geometry than selection, so editing can fail to start or start on the wrong shape. Use the same rotation-aware function in both places.

Rotation support is partial. The renderer change applies `rotate()` to every shape, and `shapeToBounds` expands the AABB for every shape. However, only the basic, image, text, wireframe and sticky plugins wrap `hitTest`. freedraw, counter, frame, group, island, connector, board-portal, community-region and chat-widget keep unrotated hit tests. `rotation` is a generic `ShapeData` field that the debug HUD, sync and AI paths can set on any shape, and any of these types with a non-zero rotation would be drawn rotated but hit-tested unrotated. Either wrap these too, or make rotation opt-in per shape definition (e.g. a `rotatable` flag) and only apply the transform/AABB expansion to opted-in types.

Gating relay/persistence on `applyClientUpdate` only works while a server-side Y.Doc exists. `applyClientUpdate` returns `true` when `doc` is `null`. The doc is created only by the AI, thumbnail and snapshot endpoints, and `destroyDoc()` runs whenever the last socket closes. So in the common case nothing is validated, and malformed payloads are still pushed into `updates`, persisted, broadcast, and replayed to every new client via `SYNC_STEP1`. `getOrCreateDoc` later just logs and skips them. Validate unconditionally, for example by applying to a lazily created doc or a throwaway doc. Also, a rejected update is dropped silently, so the sender stays permanently diverged with no error message or resync.

`trackUpdate` now persists `partition_meta`, but nothing guarantees that `loadFromStorage()` ran first. Only `fetch()` loads state; `webSocketMessage()` never awaits `loadUpdates()` or `loadFromStorage()`. If the BoardRoom is re-instantiated while hibernatable sockets (`acceptWebSocket`) stay attached, `partitionMeta` is `null` on the first update. The code then builds a fresh meta containing only the current quarter and writes it over the stored meta, orphaning every older partition. The same missing load already lets `scheduleSave` overwrite `yjs_updates` with only the post-wake updates. Have `webSocketMessage` await both loaders before mutating state, or skip persistence until loaded.

The debounce flag now resets in `finally`, after `await storage.put`, but the snapshot of `updates` is taken before the await. Any `scheduleSave()` call made while the put is in flight returns early, so those updates are not persisted until some later update schedules another save. The old code reset the flag before taking the snapshot and did not have this gap. `schedulePartitionSave` in `partition-manager.ts:43-59` has the same pattern. A failed put is also only logged and never retried. Reset the flag before taking the snapshot, and reschedule on failure.

This `withRotation` test uses a 100x100 square rotated 90°, which looks the same as the unrotated square. Both assertions would still pass if `withRotation` were a no-op or rotated the wrong way. The test therefore doesn't check that hit testing matches CSS `rotate()` (clockwise in y-down coordinates). Add a non-symmetric case, e.g. a 100x20 rect at 90° or 45°, checking a point inside only the rotated shape and a point inside only the unrotated one. There is also no test for the rotated AABB in `board-store`'s `shapeToBounds`.

This change creates several inconsistent notions of shape bounds. The spatial index and click hit tests are now rotation-aware, but marquee selection (`findShapesInRect` uses `def.getBounds`), the selection overlay and resize handles, snap, comment anchors, and `collision-utils.ts`'s own `shapeToBounds` (frame/island containment) all still use the unrotated box. For example, a rotated shape can be click-selected at a point outside its drawn selection box, and marquee selection disagrees with click selection. Consider a single shared rotation-aware bounds helper, or at least track these call sites as known follow-ups.

The new `xPreemptionDisable` check in `vTaskSwitchContext()` also blocks context switches that the task asks for itself, not only preemption. A task with preemption disabled can still call `vTaskDelay()`, block on a queue/semaphore/notification, call `vTaskSuspend(NULL)` or call `vTaskDelete(NULL)`. Each of these first takes the task off the ready list (moving it to the delayed/event/suspended/termination list) and then yields. With this check the switch is refused, so the task keeps running while its list items say it is blocked, suspended or deleted. Results: `vTaskDelay()` returns at once. `xQueueReceive()` loops back and calls `vTaskPlaceOnEventList()` again, inserting `xEventListItem` into a list it is already in. `vListInsert` has no guard against this, so the list is corrupted. `vTaskDelete(NULL)` returns to its caller, and the deleted TCB sits at the head of `xTasksWaitingTermination`, which stalls cleanup of every later deletion. Before this change these paths worked, because `prvSelectHighestPriorityTask()` picked another task, and the `vTaskPreemptionDisable()` docs do not forbid blocking. The check should apply only when the current task is still ready and running (for example `listIS_CONTAINED_WITHIN(&pxReadyTasksLists[prio], &xStateListItem)`), or be dropped in favour of the root-cause fix.

Yield requests sent to this core from another core can now hang it. `prvYieldCore()` sets the remote task's `xTaskRunState = taskTASK_SCHEDULED_TO_YIELD`. This happens in `vTaskDelete`/`vTaskSuspend` of a task running on another core, in `vTaskCoreAffinitySet`, and in the `configRUN_MULTIPLE_PRIORITIES == 0` path of `prvYieldForTask` that yields all lower-priority cores. Normally `prvSelectHighestPriorityTask()` sets the state back to `xCoreID`. The new early-return branch skips that, so the task stays in `taskTASK_SCHEDULED_TO_YIELD`. The next time it calls `taskENTER_CRITICAL()`, `prvCheckForRunStateChange()` loops forever: the yield interrupt has already been handled and refused, so nothing clears the state. The comment's promise that the yield happens on re-enable does not hold. `vTaskPreemptionEnable()` itself enters a critical section, and when called from another core it skips `prvYieldCore()` because `taskTASK_IS_RUNNING()` is false for that state. Deleting or suspending a preemption-disabled task from another core also breaks the documented rule that the task must be evicted before the critical section exits.

The 'before/after' check changes what the SMP return value means (the same pattern is at 3527-3535, 8214-8225 and 8351-8362). `prvYieldForTask()` never selects a core whose `xYieldPendings` is already set (line 932). So whenever the current core already has a legitimate pending yield, these functions now always report no yield. That pending yield can come from a previous FromISR call that passed NULL for `pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken` (explicitly supported; that is why the flag is latched), from a nested ISR, or from a deliberately separate woken variable. `portYIELD_FROM_ISR()` then does not switch, and the waiting higher-priority task is delayed until the next tick. Single-core still returns pdTRUE based on priority. `xTaskRemoveFromEventList()`'s return value drives every queue, semaphore and stream-buffer FromISR API, so the effect is wide. Since the time-slicing guard already stops the stale flag from being set, this extra layer mostly hides real pending yields. Consider dropping it, or reporting a yield whenever the flag is set and the current task is not preemption-disabled.

The new branch deliberately leaves `xYieldPendings[xCoreID] = pdTRUE` while the current task has preemption disabled, which recreates the stale flag this PR is trying to remove. `vTaskExitCritical()` reads this flag and calls `portYIELD()` on every outermost critical-section exit. As a result, each critical section a preemption-disabled task leaves now costs a full yield trap plus a refused `vTaskSwitchContext()` (taking both locks) until preemption is re-enabled. The same flag also makes `xTaskResumeAll()` report `xAlreadyYielded = pdTRUE` when no switch happened.

The ENTROPY expression has a misplaced parenthesis. It emits `F.sum(F.when(...)).otherwise(F.lit(0.0))`, which calls `.otherwise()` on an aggregate Column. Spark only allows `.otherwise()` on a Column built by `when()`, so building this Column throws IllegalArgumentException ("otherwise() can only be applied on a Column previously generated by when()") and the Layer 2B step aborts for every pipeline that uses ENTROPY, including the default test fixture. `ast.parse` cannot catch this. The intended form is `F.sum(F.when(cv > 0, -p * F.log(p)).otherwise(F.lit(0.0)))`.

MODE is implemented as `F.first(cat, ignorenulls=True)`. That returns an arbitrary, non-deterministic category (whichever row comes first after the shuffle), not the dominant one. It should pick the category with the largest aggregated value, for example `F.max_by(F.col(cat), F.col(cat_val))` or a max over `struct(cat_val, cat)`. As written, MODE features are silently wrong and can differ between runs.

RATIO emits `F.sum(col).over(frame)`, which is identical to SUM_U. A RATIO feature, which only exists with `composed_windows`, will contain a plain rolling sum under a misleading name. This is silently wrong data in the feature store. It should either compute an actual ratio (for example short-window aggregate over long-window aggregate) or raise NotImplementedError.

Three pairs of distinct operators produce byte-identical expressions: PROM_U/PROM_P (both `F.avg`), SUM_U/SUM_P (both `F.sum`) and FREQ/XM (both count non-null). The feature table gets duplicate columns under different names, so at least one operator in each pair is unimplemented while looking implemented. Implement the real semantics or raise for operators that aren't supported yet.

CREC is a windowed operator: TemporalFeature requires `window_size`, and the builder emits one feature per time window. This code ignores `w` and `direction` and always computes 1-period growth with `lag(1)`. As a result, `CREC__BACKWARD__3`, `CREC__BACKWARD__6`, etc. hold identical values.

TemporalOutputContract allows CREC, so CREC is generated for FECHA (date) measurements. For dates, `(col - lag(col)) / F.when(lag(col) != 0, lag(col))` subtracts two dates (producing an interval), divides it by a date and compares a date to 0. Spark rejects this with an AnalysisException, so Layer 3 fails for any dataset that has a FECHA measurement.

DistributionalSpaceBuilder pairs every measurement with each distributional categorical, including FECHA (date) measurements aggregated with MAX/MIN. The generated code then runs `F.sum(F.col(<cat_val>)).over(...)` and divides by that total, but Spark cannot sum dates. Any dataset with a date measurement plus a distributional categorical fails at Layer 2B. Non-numeric measurements need to be skipped or rejected.

FREQ/XM count periods where the value `isNotNull()`, and REC measures time since the last non-null value. The project docs (general_plan.md, line 108) define frequency as periods with non-zero activity. For FLAG columns (MAX(flag) = 0 when the entity had facts but the flag was off) and for zero amounts, these features count inactive months as events, and REC resets on a 0 flag. Use a non-zero / `> 0` test instead.

`generate()` overrides `AbstractCodeGenerator.generate() -> FeatureStoreOutput` but is annotated `-> object`. Under the repo's `mypy --strict` CI job this is an incompatible-override error, and every caller loses the type: the tests do `result.dag.nodes` and `result.mermaid` on an `object`. The method also checks types with `assert`, which is stripped under `-O`, and re-imports `PySparkOutput` as `_PS` although it is already imported at module level. Annotate it `-> FeatureStoreOutput` and drop the asserts and redundant imports.

These tests will fail the CI typecheck job (`mypy .` under strict). Because `generate()` returns `object`, `result.code`, `result.dag.nodes` and `result.mermaid` are attr-defined errors. At lines 325 and 353, `out.code` is read on a `CodeOutput` union without narrowing, and `SQLOutput` has no `code` attribute (union-attr error). The PR says ruff passed but says nothing about mypy.

The generated script uses a global `spark` that it never defines: it imports `SparkSession` but never creates a session. `FeatureStoreOutput.save()` writes this as `script.py`, and running it with python or spark-submit raises NameError on the first line (it only works inside a Databricks notebook). Plan 16 also says the output should be a callable that takes a SparkSession. Either emit `spark = SparkSession.builder.getOrCreate()` or wrap the script in a `def run(spark): ...`.

The docstring and PR say 'All generated transformations are lazy', but every step ends in `.write.mode('overwrite').saveAsTable(...)`, which is an eager action that materialises and overwrites a table. This contradicts the stated design and Plan 16's acceptance criterion ('All transformations are lazy until the returned callable is invoked'). Either fix the docstring or follow the design.

`AbstractDataset.source_reference` is documented as a 'Fully-qualified table name or SQL string', but every step wraps it in `spark.read.table(...)`. A SQL-string source fails at runtime. Use `spark.sql(...)` when the source is a query, or reject non-table references up front.

Identifiers and categorical values are spliced into generated Python string literals as `"{value}"` without escaping (here and in most other `F.col("...")` / alias emissions). Values from `allowed_values` or a data-derived `domain_resolver` that contain `"` or `\` produce broken or injected code. Use `repr()` consistently, as `_tbl`/`src` already do.

Two problems in this method. First, unrecognised operators silently fall through to `col.alias(...)` and emit the raw Layer 2 value as a feature, whereas `_distributional_agg_expr` raises ValueError; it should raise here too. Second, the `col_ref` conditional has identical branches, so the `isinstance` check and its local import are dead code.

The tests only check substrings and `ast.parse`, so they cannot catch runtime failures such as the ENTROPY `.otherwise` crash or wrong semantics such as MODE and RATIO. Some assertions are near-tautological: `"features" in code` always matches the '# --- Layer 3: temporal features ---' comment, and line 278 accepts nearly anything. Add at least one test that runs the generated code against a local SparkSession (guarded with `pytest.importorskip("pyspark")`) and checks metric values.

`this.eventService.isRegistered(user!, event)` is never awaited. It returns a Promise, which is always truthy, so `!promise` is always false and the 'not registered for the event' check never runs. Staff can check in any participant to any event even if that person never registered. Add `await`.

`User.findBy(...)` can return null, for example for an orphaned participant profile, but the code then uses `user!` three times. A null user crashes at `user.id` inside the service with an unhandled TypeError and a 500, not the flashed error the client expects. Handle `!user` the same way as `!profile`.

The check-then-insert is not atomic. `isCheckedIn()` and `attach()` are separate queries, and the pivot table has `unique(event_id, user_id)`, so two concurrent requests for the same participant both pass the check and the second insert throws a uniqueness error that nobody catches (500). The scanner fires many requests per QR code (see scanner.tsx), so this will happen in practice. Catch the unique violation (or use insert ... on conflict do nothing) and turn it into the 'already checked-in' error.

With `allowMultiple={true}` and `scanDelay={0}`, `onScan` runs on every frame while a code is in view. The new check-in dialog sends a POST for each callback and has no in-flight or last-slug guard. One scan produces a burst of check-in requests: duplicate inserts and 500s server-side, plus repeated error toasts. On failure the dialog stays open and keeps re-posting the same slug until the camera moves. Debounce or ignore repeats of the same slug while a request is in flight. Use a real scanDelay or `allowMultiple={false}` for this use case.

Rules of Hooks violation: the component returns early (`if (!isOpen) return null`) before calling `useTuyau()` and `useForm()`. The number of hooks therefore changes between renders as `isOpen` toggles. React lint flags this, it can cause hook-order errors, and form state is thrown away on every open. Call the hooks unconditionally and let `<Dialog open={isOpen}>` handle visibility.

The scanner trigger is rendered inside the `{!isRegistered && (...)}` block, so a staff member who is registered for the event never sees the check-in QR button. Staff visibility should not depend on the viewer's own registration. The trigger is also a bare `<QrCode>` SVG with `onClick`: it is not focusable or keyboard-operable and has no accessible label. Use a `<Button>`.

`eventID` comes straight from the request body without validation and is passed to `findOrFail`. A missing or invalid id produces a 404/exception response instead of a flashed error the dialog can show. The route is also `/events/:slug/check-in` with a participant slug as the path param under the events resource, while the event id travels in the body. Consider `/events/:id/check-in` with the slug validated in the body.

`event_id` and `user_id` are nullable and have no `onDelete('CASCADE')`, unlike the analogous `event_users` table. Rows with null keys can be inserted, and deleting a user or event that has check-ins fails the FK constraint on Postgres. Add `.unsigned().notNullable()` and `.onDelete('CASCADE')`.

`checked_in_at: new Date()` overrides the column's `defaultTo(this.now())`. With the default better-sqlite3 connection, knex binds Date as epoch milliseconds, while the column default stores a timestamp string, so stored formats are inconsistent. Rely on the DB default (or use a luxon DateTime). The `await event.save()` that follows is a no-op, because nothing on the event changed.

`await user?.load('staffProfile')` adds a DB query to every event page view, but the result is never used. `isStaff()` now reads `staffProfileId`, and the inertia shared data computes `role` separately. Remove it.

The seeder has no `app.inDev` guard, unlike `2_account_seeder.dev.ts`, so any `db:seed` run creates a staff account `staff@eneiconf.pt` with password `password`, which can check people in and collect store products. It also inserts `Department` with a hard-coded `id: 99`. On Postgres that does not advance the sequence, so a later department insert will collide when the sequence reaches 99.

This mock seeder runs on every `db:seed` with no environment guard. It silently grants a staff profile (with no department) to whatever user has id 1, which is the admin account from `2_admin_seeder`. It duplicates what `8_staff_seeder` already does and fails if no user 1 exists. Remove it or guard it to dev.

The new relations use `public checkedInUsers!:` (and `public checkedInEvents!:` in user.ts:56), while every other Lucid column and relation uses `declare`. With target ESNext / useDefineForClassFields this emits a real class field initialized on the instance. Lucid docs require `declare` so fields don't shadow ORM-managed properties. Use `declare` for consistency and safety.

`DialogContent className="h-96 w-96"` fixes the dialog at 384px. Staff will mostly scan on phones, and many are narrower than that plus padding, so the dialog overflows the viewport. The `w-64` wrapper added in scanner.tsx also shrinks the existing `/qrcode/scan` page's scanner. Use responsive sizing (e.g. `w-full max-w-sm`).

The 'Resolve source workflow run ID' step has two `env:` keys. GitHub Actions rejects duplicate mapping keys ("'env' is already defined"), so the whole workflow file fails validation and never runs: not on workflow_run and not on workflow_dispatch. The stated goal is to make this workflow run automatically, and this change leaves it unable to run at all. Delete one of the two `env:` blocks.

The run script now has `if … elif … else <old python fallback> else <new python fallback> fi`. The old fallback was left in when the new one was added. A second `else` is a bash syntax error (`syntax error near unexpected token 'else'`). Bash parses the whole `if` compound before running any of it, so once the YAML is fixed this step still fails on every trigger, including the plain workflow_run path. Remove the stale first `else` block (lines 41-93).

The `python - <<'PY'` heredocs sit inside the if/else, so after YAML strips the block indentation the terminators are `  PY` with leading spaces. A `<<'PY'` heredoc only ends on a line that is exactly `PY`. As written, the heredoc runs to end of file, bash then reports an unterminated `if` and the step fails on every event. Even with the terminator fixed, the Python body keeps a 2-space indent, so `python -` raises `IndentationError: unexpected indent`. Move the terminator and body to column 0 (or write the script to a file / use `python -c`), or put the API lookup in its own step guarded by an `if:`.

The dispatch fallback filters runs with `branch=pre-update-release`. The runs API filters on the run's head_branch. The author's own reasoning for dropping the guard is that head_branch is the default branch (`main`) for the weekly scan, which is triggered by schedule/workflow_dispatch and only checks out pre-update-release internally. This query will therefore return no runs, and both the 7-day query and the fallback query end in `SystemExit('No successful runs found…')`. Filter on the default branch, or on `event=schedule`, or drop the branch filter.

The 'prefer a run from the last 7 days' logic does nothing. Both queries ask for `per_page=1` from a list sorted newest first. If the newest successful run is inside the window, both return it. If it isn't, the fallback returns that same run. Either remove the window or make it change the result, for example by refusing or warning when the newest run is older than 7 days.

`${{ inputs.run_id }}` is interpolated straight into the shell script, which allows script injection in a job that holds an `issues: write` token. The value also isn't checked to be numeric, so it can point at any run (or another API path) that has a `weekly-security-reports` artifact. Pass it through `env:` and check it against `^[0-9]+$`.

The tracking issue is found by title alone across all open issues, which come back newest first. Anyone who can open an issue titled 'Grype remediation suggestions' becomes the target, and the bot overwrites the body of an issue that person still controls and can edit later. Match on a dedicated label and/or `creator: 'github-actions[bot]'` instead.

When a scan reports no fixable recommendations, `has_recommendations` is 'false' and the issue step is skipped. Any existing tracking issue then keeps showing the old, now-wrong recommendations. Update the issue with the 'no fixable updates' body, or close it, in that case.

The `head_branch` guard was removed with nothing in its place. Every successful run of 'Weekly Grype Security Scan' now rewrites the tracking issue, including manual dispatches from feature branches where the scan workflow may have been changed. Consider restricting to `github.event.workflow_run.event == 'schedule'` or to `head_branch == github.event.repository.default_branch`.

The underfixed gate fails any PR in which a changed vulnerable package still has a fixable High/Critical, even if the PR strictly improves security. Example: a Docker base-image bump changes many OS package versions and removes several Criticals, but one changed apk package still has a High whose fix isn't in the new image yet. The PR fails, and Dependabot base-image bumps can be blocked indefinitely. Matching is also by package name only, so two artifacts sharing a name (different type/location) can trigger it. Consider requiring that the package's own High/Critical findings did not get better (compare base vs PR per package), and key on name+type.

`recs = fixed_recommendations(pr)` is computed twice (lines 159 and 173). `fixed_high_critical_recommendations` also duplicates `fixed_recommendations` except for the severity filter. Compute once and add a severity parameter, so the two copies can't drift apart.

`if: github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'` skips the guard when a maintainer pushes a commit to a Dependabot branch: the actor becomes the maintainer and a skipped job counts as passing for required checks. The changed dependency set then merges without the Grype gate. Use `github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]'`.

The latest Grype release is looked up through the unauthenticated GitHub API, which is limited to 60 requests/hour per IP and shared across runner tenants. Dependabot opens several PRs at once on its weekly schedule, so this merge gate will fail on 403s from time to time. Send `GITHUB_TOKEN` as a bearer header, or pin a Grype version/digest so the gate is also reproducible.

`prepareForValidation` no longer returns `ownerName`, but `companySchema` (src/lib/schemas.ts:153) still requires it through `cleanString('Owner name')`. So `validationSchema.safeParse(...)` always fails in `validateAllFields`. The resulting `ownerName` error is then dropped because `fieldExistsInConfig('ownerName')` is false. The result is that 'Save Changes' in the company detail sidebar does nothing at all: `onSave` is never called and no error is shown. The schema needs updating (remove ownerName/email/phone, maybe add description) to match the new Company shape.

The Add Company form no longer has the ownerName, email and phone fields, but it still validates with `companySchema`, which requires `ownerName`. `formData.ownerName` is always undefined, so `CreationForm.handleSubmit` sets `errors.ownerName` and returns early. No field renders that error, so clicking submit silently does nothing. Before this change the submit handler at least ran.

`titleCase(item.name)` lowercases each word and then capitalises the first letter, which changes real company names: 'KSRTC' becomes 'Ksrtc', 'ABC Travels' becomes 'Abc Travels', 'McDonald' becomes 'Mcdonald'. The changed name is shown in the table, the sidebar, the avatar and the dashboard `name` query param. It is also the starting value in the edit form, so saving would write the wrong name back to the backend. Show the backend name as-is.

The status labels are now 'Verified' / 'Under Verification' / 'Suspended', but `DetailAvatarCard` only shows a status badge for 'verified', 'suspended', 'validating' or 'verifying'. Companies under verification (backend status 1) get no status badge in the detail avatar. Update the avatar card's mapping, or map the label here.

Escape only works through `<svelte:window on:keydown>`, but the dialog has `tabindex="0"` and `on:keydown|stopPropagation`. Once focus is inside the dialog, keydown events never reach the window, and that happens after any click on the map (focus moves to the nearest focusable ancestor) or after tabbing to the close button. From then on Escape does not close the modal. Handle Escape on the dialog itself or drop the stopPropagation.

`providerUrl`, `providerAttribution` and `providerMaxZoom` are never passed by `LocationMapModal`, and the component doesn't read the `tileProviders` store the way MapPreview does. So the location modal always loads public OSM tiles, ignoring the user's chosen or custom provider, and the XYZ/escapeHtml branch is dead code. The View's `maxZoom` is also hard-coded to 19 (line 110) instead of using `providerMaxZoom`.
`CircleStyle`, `Fill` and `Stroke` are imported but never used. This will fail or warn under no-unused-vars, even though the PR says linting was applied.

The shared detail sidebar now special-cases any field whose key is `location` and parses it with a hand-written regex. Every other entity that later adds a `location` field will get this behaviour whether it wants it or not, and the regex misses valid WKT such as `POINT Z (...)` or exponent notation. Make it opt-in from the config (e.g. a field type or renderer) and reuse the existing ol/format/WKT helpers in openlayers.utils.

This new view-mode `field.renderer` branch changes shared behaviour. Renderer fields used to show plain text when not being edited. Now they always mount the custom (usually editable) component, including for `editable: false` fields in edit mode. It also passes `label`/`icon`/`iconColor`/`iconBg`, which typical renderers don't declare, so Svelte logs unknown-prop warnings. Nothing in this PR uses it; consider removing it or separating view and edit renderers.
The `.location-display` selector is never used in the markup, so svelte-check reports an 'Unused CSS selector' warning.

This page-scoped `.spinner-overlay` overrides the global theme-aware rule in app.css (`rgba(var(--border-rgb), 0.6)`, z-index 2000) with hard-coded white at z-index 9999. The loading overlay now looks different from the other listing pages and shows as a white wash in dark mode. Drop the local rule and use the global one.

On mobile, 'No Companies found' shows while a fetch is in progress, including on first load, because the check is only `formattedCompanyData.length === 0`. The landmark page guards this with `!loading &&`.

The notebook calls `wg_fin.load_artifacts(...)` and `wg_fin.run_inference(...)`, but `financial_impact/financial.py` defines neither. Its docstring even says it is 'decoupled from inference and artifact loading'. The `load_artifacts` AttributeError is caught by the broad `except Exception` and printed as 'No artifacts.pkl', which hides the real cause. Execution then reaches `run_inference` (line 257, or 289 in the artifacts branch), which raises AttributeError and is re-raised, so the only code cell always fails. The committed output (an '[Errno 2] ... artifacts.pkl' message, en-dash yield ranges the code can't produce, `execution_count: null`) came from an older library version and was never re-run against this module.

`repo_root` is hardcoded to one developer's machine (`/Users/<author>/Desktop/Capstone/waferguard-ml`), so the dataset, model and output paths are wrong for everyone else. Also, `from financial_impact import financial` runs before `sys.path.insert(0, repo_root)`, so the path fix can't help the import. From `wafer_images/` the import fails unless the kernel happens to start at the repo root. Work out the root relative to the notebook (e.g. `Path.cwd().parent`) and add it to the path before importing.

Stale outputs are committed. They show a developer's local home path/username and results that don't match the current library: en-dash yield ranges, and an artifacts error message that can no longer happen. The markdown also points readers to a `waferguard.financial` library that doesn't exist; the package is `financial_impact`. Clear the outputs and fix the reference.

The 'production batch' is the whole MixedWM38 dataset, including the samples the models were trained on. The reported avg confidence (0.98), low_conf_count (49) and per-pattern financials are therefore biased and don't reflect a real lot. Use a held-out split, or label this clearly as a demo.

`compute_financials` accepts a `financial_params` override and assigns it, but never uses it. `get_params()` always reads the module-level `FINANCIAL_PARAMS`. Custom cost tables (e.g. user-tuned repair or downtime costs from the Streamlit UI) are silently ignored and the report uses the defaults. Pass `financial_params` through to `get_params`/`decompose`.

Any class ID missing from `id_to_binary` silently becomes '00000000' (Normal: 'wafer passes electrical test', $0 loss, not counted as defective). A mapping mismatch, or the notebook's `artifacts.get("id_to_binary", {})` default, would show the whole lot as clean, with understated defect rate and losses and no error. The pattern name falls back to 'Unknown' while the binary label falls back to Normal, which is inconsistent. Raise an error, or carry an explicit unknown label that isn't treated as passing.

`break_even_days` uses only `repair / daily_loss`, while EVoA also subtracts `dt * REPAIR_HOURS`. That downtime term is up to ~$19.6M, against repair costs of about $0.1–0.5M. The report contradicts itself: in the committed output, 10101010 has a 3.0-day break-even but a 30-day EVoA of -$10.9M, and 01101010 shows 0.6 days against a real payback of ~22 days. Include downtime cost in break-even so the recommendation isn't misleadingly optimistic.

The batch `avg_confidence` in the summary is an unweighted mean of per-pattern averages. A pattern with 1 wafer counts as much as one with 5,000, so the headline confidence is skewed by rare classes and isn't the average over wafers. Weight by `count`, or compute it from the raw per-wafer confidences.

With an empty batch (e.g. an uploaded .npz of shape (0, 52, 52), which passes `parse_npz_upload` validation), `rows` is empty and `pd.DataFrame([]).sort_values("priority_score")` raises KeyError. The later `if not df_financial.empty` / `df_batch.empty` guards can never run. Return early, or build the DataFrame with explicit columns.

`dominant_pattern` takes the first non-Normal row of `df_batch`, so it is only correct if the caller passes rows sorted by count descending. `build_batch_df` happens to do that, but `compute_financials` is a public API and will report the wrong pattern for any other ordering. Pick the row with max `count` (e.g. `idxmax`).

The docstring lists `CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD` as a required config key, but it is never read. `low_conf_count` (line 280) silently defaults to 0 unless the caller computes it, so the summary will show 0 low-confidence wafers unless the Streamlit integration happens to replicate the notebook's calculation.
The column is hardcoded as `evoa_30d`, but the value uses the configurable `PLANNING_HORIZON`. Any other horizon gives a mislabeled column in the CSV and UI.

Output paths are built by string interpolation of an unsanitized `batch_id`. If the Streamlit app takes the batch/lot ID from user input, values with `/` or `..` would write files outside `outdir`. Sanitize `batch_id` and use `os.path.join`.

The change removes the existing `PresentationPDFs/` and `architecture_report.pdf` ignore entries, which looks like a bad merge-conflict resolution in the 'Merge branch main' commit. Those binaries can now be committed by accident. Restore those lines next to the new entries.

Only one generated file (`reports_LOT_001/refactor_demo/batch_summary_LOT_001.json`) is ignored, but `save_reports` writes `reports_<BATCH_ID>/...` at the repo root for any batch ID. JSON reports for every other lot will appear as untracked files and may get committed. Ignore `reports_*/` instead.

This ignores `requirements.txt`, which is unrelated to the feature and surprising for a Streamlit integration: hosted deployments often rely on a committed requirements.txt. If it is meant to be a local poetry export only, document that; otherwise don't ignore it.

`appleApiKeyId` is only a local variable (declared at line 53); there is no `--apple-api-key-id` option. In a non-interactive run, iOS API Key auth therefore always reaches 'You must provide the Apple API Key ID…' and exits. That happens after the .p8 private key has already been uploaded (lines 233-240), so every CI attempt fails and leaves another orphaned key on the server. The guidance at line 212 also tells users that `--apple-api-key-file` and `--apple-issuer-id` are enough, which is wrong. Add an `appleApiKeyId` option, mention it in the error message, and check for it before uploading.

The Apple API key file is uploaded before the key ID, issuer ID and team ID are collected and before the destination is created. If the user cancels a later prompt (cancel calls process.exit), a required value is missing in CI, or `appDestinationsService.create` fails, an uploaded private key is left with no destination using it. The Google service account key upload (lines 180-187) has the same problem when destination creation fails. Collect and validate every input first, then upload the key files right before creating the destination.

Provisioning profiles are uploaded before the certificate is created. If certificate creation fails (wrong password, invalid file, network error), the uploaded profiles are left unlinked on the server. If `updateMany` fails, the certificate exists without its profiles and the command reports an error with no hint about this partial state. Create the certificate first, then upload the profiles linked to it. `CreateAppProvisioningProfileDto` already has a certificate ID field for this, which would also remove the extra PATCH.

`create` sends the form field `certificateId`, but the DTO returned by the API and `updateMany` both use `appCertificateId`. Nothing calls this path yet, so it is dead code and probably uses the wrong field name. Anyone who relies on it later may have the link silently ignored. Rename it to `appCertificateId` or remove it.

User-supplied paths go straight to `fs.readFileSync` with no existence check. This applies to the certificate here, the provisioning profiles at line 161, and the .p8/JSON key paths in destinations/create.ts. A typo throws a raw ENOENT that the top-level handler in index.ts reports to Sentry and labels 'If you think this is a bug, please open an issue'. For the certificate it also only surfaces after every prompt has been answered. Other file-taking commands check paths with `fileExistsAtPath` and print a clear error; do the same here, ideally right after each path is entered.

The keystore/p12 password and key password are read with `type: 'text'`, so they are echoed in plain text and can end up in screen recordings or shared terminal sessions. The Apple app-specific password prompt in destinations/create.ts:296 has the same problem. Use a masked input, or at least document passing secrets through flags or environment variables.

`AppDestinationDto` declares that the API returns `appleAppPassword` (types/app-destination.ts:10). `destinations:get`, and `destinations:list` (list.ts:39-41), dump the whole object with console.table or JSON, so if the API does return it, the Apple app-specific password is printed to the terminal and to CI logs. Redact secret fields before printing.

`update` takes raw `--app-apple-api-key-id` and `--app-google-service-account-key-id` IDs, while `create` takes key files and uploads them. The CLI never prints the IDs of uploaded keys and has no command to list them, so users cannot get valid values to rotate a key. Offer the same `--apple-api-key-file` and `--google-service-account-key-file` upload flow as create, and add `--apple-api-key-id` as in create.

In interactive mode, `--name` without `--platform` falls into the picker branch. The command asks for the platform, lists every certificate and ignores the name, so a user who typed `--name foo` still has to find it by hand. The same applies to certificates/get.ts:35-55 and to destinations/delete.ts and destinations/get.ts. Pass `name` to the `findAll` filter, or look it up directly once a platform is chosen.

`provisioningProfile` is the first `z.array` option in the codebase. There is no test showing that zli 0.2.0 turns a single `--provisioning-profile path` into an array rather than a string, which would fail Zod validation. The option is also accepted and uploaded for android and web certificates (line 159 has no platform check). Add a test for the flag and reject or ignore it when the platform is not iOS.

This shared helper is used by every command, and it now has a hard `limit: 50` with no pagination or search. Organizations with more than 50 apps silently cannot choose the rest. The re-fetch after creating an app (line 57) still omits the limit, so the behaviour is inconsistent. This change is also unrelated to the certificates/destinations feature.

The roughly 35-line block that resolves an ID from name/platform or an interactive picker is copied almost verbatim into certificates/get, certificates/delete, destinations/get and destinations/delete. CLAUDE.md asks for DRY code with shared utilities. Move it into a helper, for example in utils/prompt.ts, so fixes such as the ignored `--name` only need to be made once.

None of the ten new commands has tests, although sibling commands such as channels create/delete/get/list/update have them. The branchy create flows (iOS API key vs password auth, non-interactive validation, upload order) are where the bugs above are, and tests would have caught the missing API key ID option.

Nothing on the CoreSync server enforces authentication. `UseAuthorization()` only acts on endpoint metadata, and `UseCoreSyncHttpServer()` is plain middleware with no `[Authorize]` metadata, so no policy is ever checked. Even with `Auth:UseEntraId=true`, a request with no token, an expired token, or a forged token gets a failed authentication result. The request then reaches CoreSync as anonymous and can still upload and download every synced table (UserProfile, VocabularyProgress, Conversation, ...). So the claim that tokens are validated is misleading: invalid tokens are ignored, not rejected. The `RequireSyncReadWrite` policy is registered but never used. Before this ships as 'Closes #46', add a gate ahead of `UseCoreSyncHttpServer()` when Entra mode is on. That could be a `MapWhen` or middleware that calls `AuthorizeAsync` with the `sync.readwrite` policy and returns 401/403, or a fallback policy plus endpoint routing. Without it, the server only logs a failed token check.

The Entra claim lookups won't match real tokens. Microsoft.Identity.Web and JwtBearer keep `MapInboundClaims` on by default, and the inbound map renames `tid` to `http://schemas.microsoft.com/identity/claims/tenantid` and `oid` to `http://schemas.microsoft.com/identity/claims/objectidentifier`. In Entra mode, `FindFirstValue("tid")` and `FindFirstValue("oid")` will return null. TenantId then falls back to `tenant_id`, which Entra never issues, so it ends up null. UserId falls back to `NameIdentifier`, which is mapped from the pairwise `sub` claim, not `oid`. So the 'Entra ID claims take precedence' behaviour never happens, and per-user data such as vocabulary progress gets keyed by `sub` instead of the object ID. Either check both forms (`ClaimConstants.Tid`/`TenantId`, `Oid`/`ObjectId`, or `User.GetTenantId()`/`GetObjectId()`), or set `MapInboundClaims = false` on the JwtBearer options.

The auth switch fails open. `Auth:UseEntraId` defaults to false, and in that case `DevAuthHandler` signs in every anonymous caller as `dev-user`. It does this in any environment, not just Development. `appsettings.json` is gitignored and the flag only lives in `appsettings.Development.json`/AppHost, so a deployed instance missing the setting silently serves every `.RequireAuthorization()` endpoint to anyone. That includes the paid OpenAI and ElevenLabs proxies. The same pattern is copied into `src/SentenceStudio.Web/Program.cs:33-38`. Only register `DevAuthHandler` when `IsDevelopment()` (or Testing), and throw at startup if Entra is disabled anywhere else.

AppHost hardcodes `Auth__UseEntraId=false` as an environment variable on the API. Environment variables take precedence over appsettings, so the documented step of flipping `Auth:UseEntraId` to true in config has no effect when running under AppHost. An Aspire deployment would also ship the API with DevAuth turned on. Separately, the `web` (CoreSync) resource gets none of the `Auth__*`/`AzureAd__*` variables, so the API and sync server can't be switched together. Outside Development, Web would have no AzureAd section and `AddMicrosoftIdentityWebApi` would fail as soon as the flag is set. Make the flag an AppHost parameter and apply it, with the AzureAd values, to both `api` and `web`.

The sync client now sends Bearer tokens to a server it reaches over plain HTTP. The client defaults to `services__web__http__0` or `http://{host}:5240` (SentenceStudioAppBuilder.cs:56-58), and this change deletes the commented-out HTTPS/`UseHttpsRedirection` scaffolding without adding anything in its place. The token's audience is the shared API app (`api://8c05…`) with `user.read` and `sync.readwrite` scopes. Anyone sniffing the network can therefore lift a token and replay it against both the API and the sync server. Use HTTPS for the sync endpoint before tokens are attached, or make the client refuse to attach tokens to non-HTTPS URIs.

The test tokens carry the DevAuth-style claims (`tenant_id`, `NameIdentifier`, `ClaimTypes.Name`, `ClaimTypes.Email`) next to `tid`/`oid`, and real Entra access tokens have none of these. `API_ExtractsTenantContext` therefore passes through the fallback branches and hides the `tid`/`oid` mapping bug in `TenantContextMiddleware`. Also, `JwtBearerApiFactory` swaps in a plain `AddJwtBearer` instead of running the `Auth:UseEntraId=true` branch, so Microsoft.Identity.Web's real behaviour is never tested. One example: the default token here has no `scp`/`roles` claim, which Microsoft.Identity.Web rejects with IDW10201, yet these tests expect 200. Generate Entra-shaped tokens (`tid`, `oid`, `name`, `preferred_username`, `scp`) and exercise the actual Entra registration path.

`DevAuthHandler_TenantContextPopulated` and `API_ExtractsTenantContext` claim to check that `TenantContextMiddleware` extracts claims. But `/api/v1/auth/bootstrap` falls back to reading `tenant_id`, `NameIdentifier`, `Name` and `Email` straight from the `ClaimsPrincipal` (Program.cs:103-106). These tests would still pass if the middleware were removed or broken. Assert on `ITenantContext` directly, or drop the fallback from the endpoint.

The scope policies (`RequireSyncReadWrite` here; `RequireUserRead` and the others in the API) are only registered in the Entra branch. The decision docs say endpoints can 'opt into' them later. Once any endpoint calls `RequireAuthorization("RequireSyncReadWrite")`, dev mode will throw `InvalidOperationException: The AuthorizationPolicy named ... was not found`. Register the policies in both branches. In dev mode they can be no-op or authenticated-user policies.

When there's no email claim, `Email` falls back to `preferred_username`. Microsoft documents that claim as mutable, display-only, and not guaranteed to be an email address (it can be a UPN or a phone number). Treating it as the user's email risks misdirected mail or identity confusion. Leave Email null, or use the `email` optional claim.

The new Api.Tests project isn't in `src/SentenceStudio.sln`, and `.github/workflows/test.yml` only builds and tests `SentenceStudio.UnitTests`. None of the new auth integration tests run in CI, so regressions in the auth paths they cover won't be caught.

The swap replaces any ResolvedFileToPublish .dll whose file name happens to exist in `$(IntermediateOutputPath)prelink/`. It does not check whether this build wrote that file. `PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesigner` only writes assemblies it modified and never deletes old outputs, so a file left from an earlier build keeps getting swapped in. Example: a NuGet package or ProjectReference moves from a legacy MonoAndroid build that has Resource fields to a net8+/designer-assembly build (common with AndroidX/GPS package updates). The task no longer modifies it, but the old rewritten `prelink/Foo.dll` still exists. It is fed to ILLink and the app silently ships the old library code. Neither `Clean` nor `_CleanIntermediateIfNeeded` removes the per-RID inner `obj/.../<rid>/prelink` directory or the inner stamp, so this survives a clean build. Suggested fix: have the task clear OutputDirectory, or remove files it did not produce. Drive the swap from a list persisted by the task, mapping each original path to its prelink copy, and swap only items whose ItemSpec matches an original path. Remove the directory on clean.

Up-to-date checking compares only the timestamps of `@(_PreTrimmingAssembly)` against a single stamp file, so a change in the set or version of input assemblies is not detected. NuGet extracts files with the timestamp from the nupkg entry, so a newly added or upgraded package's DLL is usually older than the stamp, and the target is skipped. The new legacy library is then never rewritten: in designer-assembly mode nothing else updates its Resource field values, so resource IDs are wrong at runtime. If an older version was rewritten before, the stale prelink copy is swapped in instead (see the previous issue). The designer DLL is also an input, but it only changes when R.txt changes, so a library update with the same resources does not trigger a rerun. Changes to Xamarin.Android.Build.Tasks.dll are not tracked either. Add a hash or list file of the input item specs as an input, as is done with `_ResolvedUserAssembliesHashFile`, plus `$(MSBuildAllProjects)` or the project assets file, and add an incremental-build test that upgrades or replaces a legacy library.

The designer assembly is found only through the search directories collected from `Assemblies`. If `_Microsoft.Android.Resource.Designer.dll` is not in that list, `LoadDesigner` logs only a debug message and `ProcessAssemblyDesigner` returns false for every assembly, so the task silently does nothing. This change also removes the root descriptor that used to act as a safety net, so ILLink then trims the designer and legacy libraries keep their stale field IDs with no diagnostic. On NativeAOT this ordering really is different: `_AndroidRunNativeCompile` now pulls `_CollectPreTrimmingAssemblies` in before `_AddResourceDesignerToPublishFiles` runs, so the designer is found only if the `_FixupIntermediateAssembly` ReferenceCopyLocalPaths item happens to reach ResolvedFileToPublish. Consider passing `$(_GenerateResourceDesignerAssemblyOutput)` to the task explicitly, making `_CollectPreTrimmingAssemblies` depend on `_AddResourceDesignerToPublishFiles`, and warning when the designer cannot be resolved.

This runtime-specific file now hard-depends on `_PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesignerUpdateItems`, which is defined only in Microsoft.Android.Sdk.TypeMap.LlvmIr.targets. That file is not imported when `_AndroidTypeMapImplementation` is `trimmable`, so NativeAOT with the trimmable typemap fails with MSB4057 (target does not exist). That combination is already fragile because of the existing `_PrepareLinking` dependency, but this adds another cross-file coupling. Inject the dependency from LlvmIr.targets instead, for example with a property-based DependsOn list or `BeforeTargets="_AndroidRunNativeCompile"`.

The regenerated baselines include size changes that this change cannot cause. Native runtime binaries change in every file (libSystem.Native.so, libmonodroid.so, libclrjit.so, libcoreclr.so, libmscordaccore.so), and the Simple NativeAOT libUnnamedProject.so grows by about 15 KB.
